chapter_theme: A single song at Thirumakalam (திருமாகாளம்): after a detailed scene of lovemaking, the poet asks that, without 'who am I, who are you', he hold to the feet that took his life and chant Murugan's names daily; the praise names Murugan as the guru who gave joy and understanding to Siva.

806.reading: The poet describes lovemaking on the bed: earrings swinging, eyes wheeling like swords, ornaments slipping, hair and flowers loosened, legs entwined, anklets and garments, the nectar of the lips and a cuckoo's voice in the throat, and calls himself infatuated with such women; he asks for grace so that, without asking 'who am I, who are you', he may think anxiously on the feet that seized his life and chant daily 'Lord, Kumara, Muruga'. The praise names the vel that sent Sesha's thousand hoods, Meru, the seven seas and the Suras' bodies to dust so the earth could live, Vishnu on the serpent in the milk sea who routed Ravana's host and was friend of the five Pandavas as uncle, and Murugan the guru who gave the joy of understanding to Siva the dancer on the bull with Uma at his side, at Thirumakalam where Vishnu and devotees worship.
806.nuance: நான் ஆரு நீ எவன் எனாமல்: perhaps a plea to hold the feet without the questioning that keeps self and Lord apart, or simply without hesitation; the phrase is open. எனது ஆவி கவர் சீர்பாதம்: the feet are said to have already taken the poet's life, so the turn is to what has claimed him. Siva is called மாடேறி ஆடும் ஒரு நாதன், and Murugan the guru who gave him போதம்.
